runs.definition: agent run = one subagent (workflow agent or direct subagent); the interactive main session is counted separately; "called a model" = at least one API response with usage in its transcript

failed_or_killed.rule: outcome error (journal failed record) or killed (agent started, no result record); a killed run can still have produced files, so this is an upper bound of work not delivered by that run

resumed_workflows.rule: an agent started again under the same journal key (the workflow was resumed): both attempts are kept as runs, the first has superseded_by set; no message id is shared between them

planning.label: Planning (plan sections, gap research, critique, synthesis)

design.label: Design (UX research, design system, concepts, screens)

shell.label: Research shell, Phase A tools, samples corpus

owner_messages.rule: type user, origin.kind == "human" in the main transcript; tool results, system, meta, task-notification and peer-agent text excluded; content not read into this file; per-day counts only (no timestamps are published)

harness_cost_state.note: Claude Code's own running total for the session (last cost-state record in the main transcript); it includes model calls made inside tools (web search and fetch, run by a small model), web-search fees, and any call whose response was never written to a transcript, so it is the upper reference and the ledger the lower bound

web_search_fees.note: web-search fees and the small-model calls inside the search and fetch tools appear only in the harness's aggregate record, not in any transcript message, so they are outside cost_usd_total

basis_sentence: At API list prices (standard speed, no batch discount, prompt caching as recorded), the model usage logged in this project's agent transcripts (278 agent runs that each called a model, plus the main session, across all project phases) comes to at least US$3,542 as of 2026-11-10 20:19 UTC; that is a lower bound (web-search fees, model calls made inside tools and any response never written to a transcript are left out), the API-equivalent of work done on a subscription plan and not money spent, and the human hours are not logged.
